info.name: Gateway - LLM OpenAI-compatible errors
info.description: Exercises [policy_engine.llm_errors] disable_openai_format = false (the default) on the WSO2 API Platform gateway. Run the folders in order: Setup, the template folders, Edge cases, Known limitations, Teardown. See README.md next to this file.

variable.description: How the gateway reaches its OWN router from inside the runtime container (the LLM providers' upstream is the REST backend simulator).
Any reachable URL; the simulator's operations all respond locally and never call it.

request.description: A REST API that returns canned upstream responses through the `respond` policy. LLM providers use it as their upstream (the gateway calling itself), so backend errors can be simulated with nothing but a stock gateway. REST APIs are never reshaped, so its bodies reach the LLM provider exactly as written.
Gives the controller a moment to push the routes. If this fails, wait a few seconds and run it again.
The guardrail writes its own REST-style JSON and describes no fault. With the option on, the gateway reshapes it into the OpenAI envelope and keeps 422.

exec: pm.test("status is 422 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(422));
pm.test("error.param and error.code are always present", () => { pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("param"); pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("code"); });

item.name: Allowed request reaches the upstream untouched

exec: pm.test("status is 200 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: The upstream refuses connections, so Envoy produces the 503. The route's only policy never reads response bodies, so this also exercises the error-only body buffering.

exec: pm.test("status is 503 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(503));
pm.test("error.param and error.code are always present", () => { pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("param"); pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("code"); });
pm.test("error.code is set from the router description", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.be.a("string").and.not.empty);
pm.test("Envoy's plain-text reply is gone", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include("upstream connect error"));

item.name: Backend error WITH a body passes through (418)

exec: pm.test("status is 418 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(418));
pm.test("body passed through byte-for-byte", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.eql("{\"vendor_error\":\"I am a teapot\"}"));

item.name: Backend error already in OpenAI shape passes through (429)

exec: pm.test("status is 429 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(429));

pm.test("body passed through byte-for-byte", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.eql("{\"error\":{\"message\":\"Rate limit reached for gpt-4o in organization org-x\",\"type\":\"requests\",\"param\":null,\"code\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\"}}"));

exec: pm.test("status is 529 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(529));

pm.test("the provider sent no body, and the gateway adds none", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.eql(""));

request.description: `respond` returns 403 with `{"error":"Forbidden","message":"Caller is not allowed to use this model"}` (application/json) and no fault description. Expected: `message` beats the short `error` name.

exec: pm.test("status is 403 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test("error.param and error.code are always present", () => { pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("param"); pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("code"); });
pm.test("error.message is Caller is not allowed to use this model", () => pm.expect(body.error.message).to.eql("Caller is not allowed to use this model"));
pm.test("error.code is null (failure not classified)", () => pm.expect(body.error.code).to.be.null);

item.name: 451 /edge/unusual-status - an unusual 4xx keeps its status, type falls back to invalid_request_error

request.description: `respond` returns 451 with `{"message":"Unavailable for legal reasons"}` (application/json) and no fault description. Expected: an unusual 4xx keeps its status, type falls back to invalid_request_error.

exec: pm.test("status is 451 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(451));
pm.test("error.param and error.code are always present", () => { pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("param"); pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("code"); });
pm.test("error.message is Unavailable for legal reasons", () => pm.expect(body.error.message).to.eql("Unavailable for legal reasons"));
pm.test("error.code is null (failure not classified)", () => pm.expect(body.error.code).to.be.null);

item.name: 400 /edge/already-openai - an OpenAI-shaped policy body is left byte-for-byte

exec: pm.test("status is 400 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(400));

pm.test("body passed through byte-for-byte", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.eql("{\"error\":{\"message\":\"The model gpt-9 does not exist\",\"type\":\"invalid_request_error\",\"param\":\"model\",\"code\":\"model_not_found\"}}"));
pm.test("the author's param and code survive", () => { const e = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(e.param).to.eql("model"); pm.expect(e.code).to.eql("model_not_found"); });

item.name: 409 /edge/nested-error-message - a body with a string error.message is already readable, left as-is

request.description: The formatter treats any body whose `error.message` is a string as OpenAI-shaped: an SDK can read it, and reshaping could only lose fields its author set.

exec: pm.test("status is 409 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(409));
pm.test("body passed through byte-for-byte", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.eql("{\"error\":{\"message\":\"Conflict on resource\",\"reason\":\"x\"}}"));

item.name: 200 /edge/success - a successful response is never touched

exec: pm.test("status is 200 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Accept: application/xml still gets the OpenAI JSON

request.description: An OpenAI SDK reads only the OpenAI envelope, so Accept is ignored on LLM routes.

exec: pm.test("status is 403 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
pm.test("error.param and error.code are always present", () => { pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("param"); pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("code"); });
pm.test("error.message is Caller is not allowed to use this model", () => pm.expect(body.error.message).to.eql("Caller is not allowed to use this model"));
pm.test("error.code is null (failure not classified)", () => pm.expect(body.error.code).to.be.null);

item.name: Streaming request (stream: true) still gets a JSON error

request.description: Errors are returned before the stream opens, as a plain JSON body, like the reference API.

pm.test("error.param and error.code are always present", () => { pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("param"); pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("code"); });
pm.test("status is 403 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

pm.test("error.param and error.code are always present", () => { pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("param"); pm.expect(body.error).to.have.property("code"); });

item.name: REST API errors are NOT reshaped

request.description: The option is scoped to LlmProvider/LlmProxy. The same kind of body on a REST API stays as written.

exec: pm.test("status is 418 (never changed by the formatter)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(418));
pm.test("body passed through byte-for-byte", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.eql("{\"vendor_error\":\"I am a teapot\"}"));

pm.test("body is NOT the OpenAI envelope", () => { let j = null; try { j = JSON.parse(pm.response.text()); } catch (e) {} pm.expect(j && j.error && typeof j.error === "object" && "type" in j.error && "param" in j.error).to.not.be.ok; });

item.name: Unmatched route is NOT reshaped (no API, so no API kind)
